claims.text:
Corporate Documents Required from the Sponsoring PT PMA:
The company acts as the mandatory sponsor and must provide robust corporate compliance records [4, 5]:
   NIB (Nomor Induk Berusaha): Must be active in the OSS system and contain the KBLI (business sector code) matching the director's specific job title [4, 6].
   Deed of Establishment & Amendments (Akta Pendirian PT + Perubahan terakhir): Accompanied by the Ministry of Law and Human Rights approval decree (SK Kemenkumham) [4, 5].
   Company Tax ID (NPWP Perusahaan) [4, 5].
   WLKP (Wajib Lapor Ketenagakerjaan Perusahaan): A mandatory and up-to-date company employment report [5].
   BPJS Ketenagakerjaan Report: Proof of active social security enrollment for the company's local Indonesian employees [5].
   Company Organizational Chart (Bagan Organisasi): Visually demonstrating the foreign director's position within the company hierarchy [4, 7].
   Statement of Companion Worker (Surat Pernyataan Pendampingan): A formal commitment to appoint a local Indonesian worker (TKI Pendamping) for knowledge transfer [4].
   Approved RPTKA (Rencana Penggunaan Tenaga Kerja Asing): The formal work authorization plan approved by Kemnaker, which replaced the physical IMTA document [1, 8].

    "answer": "The standard timeline to incorporate a Foreign Investment Limited Liability Company (PT PMA) and obtain operational readiness in Indonesia currently ranges from 2 to 4 weeks [1, 2]. The process follows a strict sequence governed by the Company Law (UU No. 40 of 2007) and the updated Risk-Based Licensing framework (PP No. 28 of 2025), which is a major post-Omnibus Law reform that shifted Indonesia from a fragmented permit-based system to a centralized continuous compliance model [3-5]. \n\nHere are the precise steps for PT PMA incorporation:\n\n**Step 1: Deed of Establishment (Akta Pendirian)**\nA local notary drafts the incorporation deed in Indonesian, detailing the company name, capital structure, shareholders, directors, commissioners, and intended business activities (KBLI codes) [6]. This notary phase typically takes 3 to 5 days [1, 2].\n\n**Step 2: Ministry of Law Approval (SK Kemenkumham)**\nThe notary submits the deed via the AHU Online system to obtain the SK Kemenkumham, which officially grants the PT PMA its status as a separate legal entity (badan hukum) [4, 7]. This approval process takes 5 to 10 working days [1, 2]. \n\n**Step 3: Corporate Tax ID (NPWP Badan)**\nThe company must register for its tax identification number at the local tax office, which takes 1 to 2 days [1, 2, 7]. \n\n**Step 4: Registration via OSS (NIB Issuance)**\nPost-Omnibus Law, the Online Single Submission (OSS) system serves as the sole gateway for business licensing [8, 9]. By inputting the SK Kemenkumham data, declaring your investment plan, and selecting your KBLI codes, the system automatically generates the Business Identification Number (NIB) instantly [1, 10, 11]. Whenever you select a code, you must verify its foreign investment status under the Positive Investment List (Perpres No. 10 of 2021); for example, registering a restaurant under KBLI 56101 is classified as TERBUKA (100% open to PMA) [10, 12]. \n\n**Step 5: Sectoral Licenses (Perizinan Berusaha)**\nUnder the PP 28/2025 framework, subsequent licensing requirements depend entirely on the risk profile of your KBLI [5, 13, 14]. Low-risk activities only need the NIB to operate, medium-low requires an NIB plus a Self-Declared Standard Certificate, medium-high requires a Verified Standard Certificate (which currently takes 5 to 14 days for government verification), and high-risk activities require a formal License (Izin) [1, 5, 13, 15]. \n\n**Step 6: Corporate Bank Account Opening**\nThe company must open a bank account strictly under the PT PMA's name, a process that takes 3 to 7 days [1, 2, 16]. Following the post-Omnibus Law updates in BKPM Regulation No. 5 of 2025, the mandatory minimum paid-up capital of IDR 2.5 billion must be deposited into this account and locked for 12 months for operational use [17-19].",

    "answer": "As an expatriate holding a KITAS (Limited Stay Permit) in Indonesia, your tax obligations depend heavily on your classification as either a Resident Taxpayer (SPDN - *Subjek Pajak Dalam Negeri*) or a Non-Resident Taxpayer (SPLN - *Subjek Pajak Luar Negeri*) [1]. Under Indonesian tax law, holding a KITAS or staying in Indonesia for more than 183 days within a 12-month period establishes your intention to reside, classifying you as an SPDN [2-4]. Conversely, foreigners staying 183 days or less without the intent to reside are classified as SPLN [1, 5]. \n\nBecause a KITAS holder qualifies as an SPDN, you are legally required to register for a Personal Taxpayer Identification Number (NPWP Pribadi) as soon as you meet the subjective and objective tax requirements, in accordance with the General Provisions and Tax Procedures Law (KUP - UU No. 28/2007, as amended by the HPP Law No. 7/2021) [6, 7].\n\nAs an SPDN, you are subject to Article 21 Income Tax (PPh 21) at progressive rates ranging from 5% to 35% on your worldwide income [8-11]. Your employer (such as a PT PMA) will withhold this monthly using the Effective Average Rate (TER) system introduced by PMK 168/2023 [11]. If you were instead classified as an SPLN, you would be subject to Article 26 Income Tax (PPh 26)—a flat 20% withholding tax exclusively on your Indonesian-sourced income, subject to potential reductions via Double Tax Avoidance Agreements (P3B) [9, 12]. Notably, eligible foreign SPDNs with specific expertise can benefit from a 4-year territorial tax exemption, meaning they are only taxed on Indonesian-sourced income for their first four years, provided they do not claim tax treaty benefits [13-16].\n\n**CoreTax System Changes to Note:**\nYou must also comply with the new CoreTax Administration System (PSIAP) implemented under PMK 81/2024, which fundamentally changes how expats interact with the Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) [17, 18]. \n*   **16-Digit NPWP Format:** Under PMK 112/2022, while Indonesian citizens now use their National Identity Number (NIK) as their tax ID, foreign nationals (WNA) are issued a specific 16-digit NPWP format by the DJP [19-22]. \n*   **Digital Integration:** The new CoreTax portal centralizes all tax administration, replacing the legacy DJP Online portal and eliminating the need for the old EFIN (Electronic Filing Identification Number) for login authentication [23-25]. query: Can a foreign investor own land under HGB title through PT PMA?

  "value": {
    "answer": "Yes, a foreign investor can legally acquire and hold land under the **Hak Guna Bangunan (HGB - Right to Build)** title by establishing a **PT PMA (Penanaman Modal Asing)**, which is a foreign-owned Indonesian limited liability company [1, 2]. \n\nBecause foreign individuals and entities are strictly prohibited from holding freehold titles (**Hak Milik / SHM**), using a PT PMA to hold an HGB certificate is the most powerful and secure legal structure for commercial investments and property portfolios in Indonesia [3, 4].\n\nHere is how the HGB title through a PT PMA works, along with the critical legal steps you must take:\n\n**1. Duration and Title Security**\nUnder **PP 18/2021**, the HGB title grants your company the right to build and own structures on the land for a total maximum duration of **80 years** [5, 6]. This is divided into an initial term of 30 years, an extension of 20 years (which must be requested before the initial term expires), and a final renewal of 30 years [5, 7]. The HGB is an official land title registered at the National Land Agency (BPN), meaning it provides strong legal protection and can even be used as collateral for bank financing (Hak Tanggungan) [8, 9].\n\n**2. PT PMA Capital Requirements (2025 Updates)**\nRecent regulatory updates under **BKPM Regulation 5/2025** have made this structure significantly more accessible. The minimum paid-up capital requirement for a PT PMA has been drastically reduced from IDR 10 billion down to **IDR 2.5 billion** (approx. USD 150,000) [10, 11]. While your total intended investment plan must still reach IDR 10 billion, the value of the land and buildings you purchase now legally counts toward that total requirement [10, 12].\n\n**3. Mandatory RTRW Zoning Verification (Zonasi)**\nBefore you commit to buying any HGB land or forming your PT PMA, you **must verify the spatial zoning (RTRW / RDTR Bali)** for the specific plot [13, 14]. \n*   If your PT PMA intends to operate a commercial accommodation (like a villa rental or hotel), the land must be located in a **Pink Zone (Kawasan Pariwisata / Tourism)** or an applicable commercial zone [15, 16]. \n*   Purchasing land in a **Green Zone (Kawasan Pertanian / Agriculture)** with the intent to build is strictly prohibited [17, 18]. You will be denied building permits (PBG) and could face forced demolition [17, 18]. Always obtain a formal *Surat Informasi Tata Ruang (SITR)* or *KKPR* via the OSS system to confirm the zoning before any transaction [19, 20].\n\n**4. The Role of the PPAT**\nWhen your PT PMA is ready to acquire the HGB title, the transaction must be executed through a **PPAT (Pejabat Pembuat Akta Tanah - Land Deed Official)** [21]. A standard Notary (*Notaris*) cannot legally transfer land titles; you must use a PPAT who holds specific jurisdiction in the exact Regency (Kabupaten) where the land is located (e.g., Badung or Gianyar) [21, 22].\n\n**5. Warning: Strictly Avoid Nominee Structures**\nYou must never attempt to buy freehold land (Hak Milik) using an Indonesian citizen as a \"nominee\" [23]. Nominee structures are explicit legal fraud intended to bypass Indonesia's Basic Agrarian Law and are considered **null and void by law** (*batal demi hukum*) [24]. Furthermore, under Bali's new **Perda No. 4/2026**, engaging in a nominee arrangement is now a criminal offense carrying penalties of up to 5 years in prison and fines of IDR 1 billion for both the foreigner and the local nominee [25]. \n\nIf you do not wish to invest the capital required for a PT PMA, your only other legal alternatives are **Hak Pakai (Right to Use)**—which allows an individual foreigner with a valid residency visa (KITAS/KITAP) to hold residential property for up to 80 years—or a notarized long-term **Leasehold (Hak Sewa)** contract [26, 27].",

  "value": {
    "answer": "Il **LKPM** (Laporan Kegiatan Penanaman Modal) è il rapporto periodico obbligatorio sulle attività di investimento che tutte le società, incluse le PT PMA, devono presentare al Ministero degli Investimenti (BKPM) [1], [2]. A seguito dei cambiamenti introdotti dalla Omnibus Law (UU 11/2020 sui Cipta Kerja) e dal PP 5/2021, la gestione del LKPM è stata interamente digitalizzata e integrata all'interno del sistema OSS-RBA (Online Single Submission Risk-Based Approach) [3], [4]. \n\nQuesto strumento normativo permette al governo indonesiano di monitorare la realizzazione dei capitali, lo stato di avanzamento dei progetti e l'assolvimento degli obblighi operativi [1], [5]. Ai fini della compliance, nel LKPM è obbligatorio rendicontare dettagliatamente l'assorbimento occupazionale, distinguendo rigorosamente tra lavoratori locali (WNI) e lavoratori stranieri (WNA) [6], [7], [5], [8]. Questo dato incrociato permette alle autorità di verificare il rispetto dei rapporti di impiego e l'efficacia del piano di trasferimento di competenze richiesto per i WNA [8].\n\n**Scadenze di presentazione aggiornate al 2025/2026**\nPoiché le PT PMA sono automaticamente classificate come imprese di grandi dimensioni, essendo soggette a un vincolo di investimento superiore a 10 miliardi di IDR, sono obbligate a presentare il LKPM con cadenza trimestrale [9], [10], [11]. \n\nCon l'entrata in vigore del recente Regolamento BKPM n. 5 del 2025, la scadenza per l'invio è stata estesa dal 10 al **15 del mese successivo al trimestre di riferimento** [12], [13], [14]. Il calendario esatto è il seguente:\n*   **Q1 (Gennaio – Marzo):** entro il 15 Aprile [15], [16].\n*   **Q2 (Aprile – Giugno):** entro il 15 Luglio [15], [16].\n*   **Q3 (Luglio – Settembre):** entro il 15 Ottobre [15], [16].\n*   **Q4 (Ottobre – Dicembre):** entro il 15 Gennaio dell'anno successivo [15], [16].\n\n**Avvertenze operative e sanzioni**\nL'obbligo di presentare il LKPM scatta dal trimestre successivo all'emissione del NIB nel portale OSS [17], [18]. È un errore comune credere che in assenza di ricavi o in fase pre-operativa non sia necessario fare reporting: la legge impone di presentare il LKPM indicando la fase di preparazione (*Persiapan*) e segnalando investimenti \"Nihil\" (zero) se non ci sono state spese [19], [20], [21], [17]. \n\nIl mancato invio tramite OSS RBA innesca un sistema di sanzioni automatiche che parte da lettere di diffida (SP1 e SP2) fino ad arrivare al blocco del profilo OSS e alla revoca del NIB [22], [23]. Un NIB bloccato paralizza l'operatività della PT PMA, impedendo l'emissione o il rinnovo dei permessi di lavoro (RPTKA/KITAS) per i WNA, ostacolando l'aggiornamento dei dati obbligatori della previdenza sociale (BPJS Ketenagakerjaan e Kesehatan), e precludendo qualsiasi modifica societaria [9], [22], [24].",

    "answer": "Under the post-Omnibus Law framework (UU 6/2023 on Job Creation), the licensing process for a PT PMA in Bali is governed by Government Regulation (PP) No. 28 of 2025, which recently replaced PP 5/2021 [1, 2]. The OSS-RBA (Online Single Submission Risk-Based Approach) system dictates your required licenses based on your business activities.\n\n**1. Basic Requirements (Persyaratan Dasar)**\nBefore obtaining operational licenses, a PT PMA must fulfill fundamental prerequisites [1, 3]:\n*   **KKPR (Conformity of Spatial Utilization):** Zoning approval ensuring your business matches Bali's spatial planning (RDTR) [4, 5].\n*   **PL (Environmental Approval):** Environmental documents like SPPL or UKL-UPL [4, 5].\n*   **PBG & SLF (Building Approval & Certificate of Worthiness):** Ensures the building is legally constructed and safe to operate [4, 5].\n*   *Post-Omnibus Update:* Under PP 28/2025, if your PT PMA leases space in a commercial building (e.g., a mall or office complex) that already holds these permits, you are exempt from applying for them individually and can simply upload your lease agreement and the property manager's NIB [4, 6].\n\n**2. Risk-Based OSS Licenses**\nOnce basic requirements are met, OSS issues licenses based on the risk level of your registered KBLI (Business Classification Code) [7]:\n*   **Low Risk:** Requires only a Business Identification Number (NIB). Operations can commence immediately [8].\n*   **Medium-Low Risk:** NIB + Self-Declared Standard Certificate [8, 9].\n*   **Medium-High Risk:** NIB + Verified Standard Certificate (requires technical verification before full operations) [8, 9].\n*   **High Risk:** NIB + Full Business License (Izin) + Standard Certificate, requiring full approval from the relevant ministry before commercial activities begin [8, 9].\n\n**3. BPJS Obligations (Social Security & Healthcare)**\nThe issuance of your NIB automatically acts as your company's initial registration for **BPJS Kesehatan** and **BPJS Ketenagakerjaan** [10, 11]. However, compliance differs strictly between local and foreign staff:\n*   **WNI (Indonesian Citizens):** Registration for all BPJS programs (JKK, JKM, JHT, JP, JKP) and Healthcare is mandatory from the first day of employment [12].\n*   **WNA (Foreign Workers):** Mandatory enrollment applies only to WNA holding a Work KITAS and employed in Indonesia for more than six months [13, 14].\n*   *Post-Omnibus Update:* The OSS system is now highly integrated with government databases, including the DJP Coretax system. If your PT PMA fails to properly enroll WNI or eligible WNA employees in BPJS, the system will flag the discrepancy, blocking your ability to renew OSS licenses or file your mandatory quarterly LKPM reports [15, 16].\n\n**4. UU Ketenagakerjaan (Manpower Law) & Operations**\nTo legally operate and hire staff, your PT PMA must comply with the Manpower Law (UU 13/2003 as amended by UU 6/2023):\n*   **WNI Employees:** You must file the Mandatory Manpower Report (WLKP) via the SIAPkerja portal within 30 days of hiring your first employee [17, 18]. Employees must be paid in accordance with the 2026 Bali Minimum Wage (UMP/UMK), which currently peaks at IDR 3,791,002.57 for the Badung regency [19].\n*   **WNA Employees:** The Omnibus Law formally abolished the standalone IMTA document. To hire foreign experts, the PT PMA must now obtain an approved **RPTKA (Foreign Worker Utilization Plan)** through the TKA-Online system, which serves as the work permit authorization [20, 21]. Employers must pay the DKPTKA fee of USD 100/month [22, 23] and must appoint a WNI counterpart (*TKI Pendamping*) to facilitate knowledge transfer (exempt for Directors/Commissioners) [24, 25]. Furthermore, WNA are strictly prohibited under the Manpower Law from occupying HR or Personnel management roles [26].",

query: What are the differences between PT PMA and PT PMDN for a foreign investor wanting to do business in Bali?

  "value": {
    "answer": "As an expert in Indonesian company formation and foreign investment, here are the critical differences between a PT PMA and a PT PMDN for a foreign investor looking to operate in Bali, governed by the Company Law (UU 40/2007), the Investment Law (UU 25/2007), and the updated Risk-Based Licensing framework (PP 28/2025).\n\n**1. Ownership Limitations and Legality**\n*   **PT PMA (Perseroan Terbatas Penanaman Modal Asing):** This is the only legal corporate vehicle that permits foreign ownership in Indonesia [1]. Depending on the specific business sector, a foreign investor can own up to 100% of the shares in a PT PMA [2, 3].\n*   **PT PMDN / PT Lokal (Penanaman Modal Dalam Negeri):** This structure is strictly reserved for Indonesian citizens (WNI) and 100% domestic entities [4-6]. Foreigners are strictly prohibited from holding shares in a PT PMDN [4-6]. Attempting to bypass this restriction using a local nominee agreement is illegal under Indonesian law, offering the foreign investor zero legal protection over the assets and exposing them to severe regulatory and immigration sanctions [7, 8]. \n\n**2. Permitted Sectors and KBLI PMA Status**\nUnder the Positive Investment List (Perpres No. 10/2021, as amended by Perpres No. 49/2021), all business activities are mapped to KBLI codes and categorized by their openness to foreign investment [2, 9]. A PT PMA can only operate in sectors classified as **TERBUKA** (Open) or **TERBATAS** (Restricted), whereas a PT PMDN can operate across all domestic sectors [6, 10]. \n*   **TERBUKA (100% PMA):** Sectors fully open to foreign investors. Examples include **KBLI 55193 / 55194 (Vila)** and **KBLI 56101 (Restoran)**, which allow 100% foreign ownership [11-13]. \n*   **TERBATAS (Capped PMA):** Sectors where foreign ownership is limited and mandates a joint venture with a local partner. For instance, **KBLI 73100 (Aktivitas Periklanan / Advertising)** is TERBATAS and capped at a maximum of 49% foreign ownership [14].\n*   **TERTUTUP (0% PMA):** Sectors completely closed to foreigners and reserved for PT PMDN/Indonesian citizens. A prime example in Bali is **KBLI 55130 (Pondok Wisata / Homestay)**, which is TERTUTUP and cannot be operated by a PT PMA under any circumstances [11, 15].\n\n**3. Capital Requirements (Post-Omnibus Law Updates)**\nThe Omnibus Law (UU 6/2023) and the recently enacted BKPM Regulation No. 5 of 2025 introduced strict capitalization rules to filter out underfunded foreign investments.\n*   **PT PMA:** The total investment commitment must exceed IDR 10 billion per 5-digit KBLI code and per project location, explicitly excluding the value of land and buildings [16, 17]. Post-Omnibus Law, the minimum paid-up capital (Modal Disetor) has been reduced to IDR 2.5 billion [16, 17]. However, BKPM Reg 5/2025 introduces a mandatory \"capital locking\" rule: this IDR 2.5 billion must be deposited into the corporate bank account and remain locked for a minimum of 12 months, accessible only for legitimate operational and capital expenditures (e.g., equipment, facility development, salaries) [9, 18-20]. \n*   **PT PMDN:** The capitalization thresholds are drastically lower. A PT Lokal only requires a minimum authorized capital (Modal Dasar) of IDR 50 million, with a minimum paid-up capital of IDR 12.5 million (25% of authorized capital) [6, 21]. \n\n**4. Management and Visas**\nWhile a foreigner cannot own shares in a PT PMDN, they can legally serve as a Director (Direktur) or Commissioner (Komisaris) in one, provided they hold a valid working KITAS sponsored by the company [6, 22]. In a PT PMA, a foreign shareholder who injects a minimum personal capital placement of IDR 1 billion is eligible to apply for an Investor KITAS (E28), which facilitates residency without the need to pay the monthly DKPTKA foreign worker tax [23-25].\n\n**5. Licensing and Compliance (OSS RBA and LKPM)**\nFollowing the transition to PP 28/2025 (which revoked PP 5/2021), both entities utilize the Online Single Submission (OSS) system for Risk-Based Licensing [26]. However, the continuous compliance burden is significantly heavier for a PT PMA. A PT PMA is mandated to file the *Laporan Kegiatan Penanaman Modal* (LKPM) quarterly to prove the steady realization of their IDR 10 billion investment commitment [27-29]. Under the post-Omnibus Law updates in BKPM Reg 5/2025, the deadline for this LKPM reporting has been shifted to the 15th of the following month [30]. Failure to submit these reports allows the OSS system to automatically flag the entity, leading to the suspension or revocation of the Business Identification Number (NIB) and subsequent operational shutdowns [30, 31].",
